reason: E3 directly supports that a large electronegativity difference strengthens the alloy, which underpins the mechanism. However, no cited evidence supports the specific claims that Mo increases electronegativity difference in this alloy, that V substitution reduces it, or that this improves dislocation mobility and plasticity while retaining strength. E1, E2, and E4 are irrelevant to these premises.
premises: High Mo content in NbZrTiHfMo increases electronegativity difference, which restricts dislocation mobility and reduces plasticity.
Reducing electronegativity difference by substituting Mo with V will lower the barrier to dislocation motion and enhance plasticity.
The substitution will preserve the disordered BCC structure and maintain high solution strengthening, retaining yield strength near 1719 MPa.
An electronegativity difference contributes to strengthening in high-entropy alloys.
